description: A C# game engine in which a program opens a window, draws each frame with plain static calls named as raylib's functions are, and draws Dear ImGui in the same frame, over SDL3, Vulkan and Slang, with an ECS and source-generated behaviors underneath.
releaseNotes:
The soak step starts its games three seconds apart and gives each five minutes to serve through E3D_OPEN_WAIT, which build/open-game.sh reads, saying how long each took, so nineteen games sharing a runner's four cores are not failed for a slow start.
The feature test's audio zone says its sounds are not heard yet until the music has played over a second and the rest hold, within a bound of frames after which it says what fell short, and the drive reads it until then, so a runner whose frames come slowly is judged on the music it played.
A program leaves global illumination's screen probes out with SetGlobalIlluminationScreenProbes, so they are neither made nor traced for the window or a render texture and every surface reads the cascades' light alone, the guide giving what that saves with and without glow lights.
The first gamepad moves through ImGui only once a program calls SetImGuiGamepadNavigation, as ImGui and rlImGui leave it, so a game played by the pad keeps its presses while a tool window is open, with Manor and the feature test's panel turning it on and the interface zone pressing the pad before any click.
The feature test gains a scenes zone, which starts a level as a saved game and reads it back with its data found by id after a rename, and an interface zone of screens, typed text, ImGui and a gamepad, each read back by the drive.
A sound placed by its position is panned toward the side of the listener it is on and grows quieter from its near distance to silence at its far one, through a spatial processor the engine installs by default, as the audio guide says.
The feature test gains an audio zone, which reads a drone panned toward its speaker in the mix and a wave written and read back, and a text zone, which reads back a page of Lato, Hebrew and a colour glyph.
The feature test gains a room that reads global illumination on and off in the window, a particles zone that counts each emitter in a texture, and an effects zone that reads each effect in the window and its shaders back.
The feature test gains a models zone, whose arm is read back as it bends and whose robot runs a state machine it names by id, and a lights zone, whose lamp, spot, shadow and glow are read on its floor from above.
The feature test gains an admin panel in ImGui that reads the frame's costs and turns the engine's and each zone's features on and off, and a crash file beside it that the next run names, each read back by the drive and the games job.
A feature test beside the games puts the engine's areas on one map a capsule character walks, its hub and its drawing and course zones first, each saying in a status line what it read back, walked in the games job and soaked and resized with the games.
A struct marked DataAsset is kept in a file of its own with an id given at its first save, and a component's DataRef names the file by that id, found again after a rename, as data many entities share needs.
A character flies at the velocity it is given with gravity held off and walls and ceilings still stopping it, as a creative mode needs, and PlacePhysicsBody puts a body somewhere at rest where SetPhysicsBodyPosition keeps its velocity, as a respawn needs.
A system asks to run before or after another of its stage by name or in a chain, which the app sorts each stage by as it starts, refusing a missing name or a round by name, and which the batches and the shuffle keep.
title: 3DEngine
